observed.description: ServerSubagentLifecycle.rebind_pool_and_drain publishes the replacement entrypoint before the retired entrypoint drains. Each NotionAccountPool instance owns its own per-slot busy flag. A refreshed pool built from the same logical accounts therefore starts with no knowledge that an old-generation child still holds account-A.
observed.current_test_contract: The existing drain test explicitly requires a new child to run on the replacement entrypoint while the old generation is still active, but fake entrypoints do not model overlapping logical account identities.
observed.reservation_gap: The shared reserved_account_ids callback protects foreground parent reservations; it does not expose the account currently leased by a retired delegated child, so it cannot bridge busy state between pool generations.
observed.offline_reproduction: Two independent pool instances containing the same logical account-A were placed behind publish-before-drain semantics. Old generation held account-A while the replacement generation selected account-A concurrently; observed peak logical-account concurrency=2.

risk: One legitimate Notion account can receive concurrent delegated provider work through two pool generations during auth/runtime refresh.
Per-pool busy serialization and cooldown accounting are bypassed across generations even though each pool is individually correct.
If either child owns a remote thread/tool chain, cross-generation overlap can create rate-limit pressure or inconsistent account-scoped state exactly during recovery/rebind.

recommended_contract.minimum_safe_option: During rebind_pool_and_drain, do not admit replacement-generation delegated launches until all retired-generation delegated children have drained; then publish the replacement entrypoint.
recommended_contract.higher_concurrency_option: If immediate publication is required, propagate exact active delegated account ids from retired generations into replacement reservation avoidance until each old lease releases. This requires explicit account-id exposure from the adapter/lifecycle and must not infer provider thread affinity.
recommended_contract.required_regression: Old and new pools contain the same logical account-A. While old child holds A, a new child must not begin provider work on A. After old release, new child may use A. Different non-overlapping logical accounts may still proceed if the chosen design proves that safely.
